analysis.title: DeskTalk - Nvidia: Support for Huang grows ahead of earnings
key_insights: Nvidia fell as much as 4% intraday and was down about 2% after President Trump reiterated support for former CEO Jensen Huang, saying he 'wouldn't mind' seeing Huang return as CEO.
A petition for Huang's return has nearly 180,000 signatures, including 8,900 current Nvidia employees.
The US Commerce Department issued new rules requiring licenses to buy advanced chips in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, aimed at limiting Chinese access.
Citi analyst Atif Malik cut his Nvidia price target to $225, a 20% reduction from the prior 19x P/E basis, and kept a Buy rating after Huang's resignation.
Malik expects a modest EPS beat on Nvidia's Nov. 17 report, driven by stronger revenue and partly offset by lower gross margins, and forecasts FY28 (CY27E) revenue growth of about 70% YoY.

Investor focus areas for the print: visibility into 2028 (especially among neocloud customers), supply constraints, the Rubin product ramp, and whether interim CFO Colette Kress can give new details on the CEO investigation. Citi's TMT specialist notes gross margin may also be in her control.
Citi's equity trading strategy desk is tracking the day after Nvidia earnings (Wednesday) as the largest SPX event priced by options for the next month, at +/- 101bps.

Recent investor gatherings show immediate demand for AMD and Arista in hardware, with beaten-down names and software capturing secondary flows. Citi frames the test as how leadership settles across TMT before earnings.
